name: aob_find
title: Find byte patterns
description: Find up to 8 array-of-bytes patterns (hex bytes and ?? wildcards) and report each pattern's matches, whether the count is exact and whether it is unique. Each pattern is one Cheat Engine scan that blocks Cheat Engine while it runs: without module or startAddress/endAddress it scans the whole target, so scope it, and use executable=required for code. Uniqueness needs limit 2 or more.

patterns.description: The patterns, 1 to 8, each up to 4096 byte positions, such as 48 8B ?? ?? ?? ?? 89 43 10.

module.description: Scan only this loaded module's image, such as game.exe; faster and cannot match in another module.

startAddress.description: The first allowed match address or expression; requires endAddress.

endAddress.description: The last allowed match address or expression; requires startAddress.

writable.description: Whether matches must be in writable memory: required, excluded or any (default).

executable.description: Whether matches must be in executable memory: required, excluded or any (default).

copyOnWrite.description: Whether matches must be in copy-on-write memory: required, excluded or any (default).

alignment.description: Only match addresses divisible by this number, such as 4; not with lastDigits.

lastDigits.description: Only match addresses whose hexadecimal form ends with these 1 to 16 digits; not with alignment.

limit.description: The most matches to list per pattern, 1 to 10000.

results.description: One entry per requested pattern, in request order.

pattern.description: The pattern as scanned: uppercase byte pairs and ?? wildcards separated by single spaces.

exact.description: Whether count is proven to be every match in scope; false when the limit cut the list or Cheat Engine cannot tell zero matches from a failure.

unique.description: Whether exactly one match exists in scope: exact and count 1. Use a limit of at least 2.

scope.description: What Cheat Engine scanned: bounded_scan (only the module or range), global_scan, filtered_global_scan (whole target, then filtered) or unknown.

targetVerified.description: Whether the matches belong to one confirmed target incarnation for the whole scan.

elapsedMs.description: How long Cheat Engine's scan and the copy of its result took, in milliseconds.

matches.description: The match addresses in Cheat Engine's order, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

name: aob_generate_signature
title: Generate an AOB signature
description: Generate an array-of-bytes signature that finds an address inside a loaded module (Cheat Engine's getUniqueAOB), then verify it with a separate scan of that module. The address must be inside a module of at most 64 MiB; others are refused because Cheat Engine would scan the whole address space. Blocks Cheat Engine while it scans; review the pattern and mask displacements before relying on it.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression inside a loaded module, such as game.exe+1C0.

module.description: The module that must contain the address; defaults to the module that contains it.

verify.description: Whether to verify the signature with a separate bounded scan of the module.

address.description: The resolved address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

module.description: The module that contains the address and was scanned.

unique.description: Whether the signature matches only once in the module: proven by the verification scan when verified is true.

verified.description: Whether a separate bounded scan of the module checked the signature.

pattern.description: The signature, uppercase byte pairs and ?? wildcards; omitted when Cheat Engine found no unique signature.

patternStart.description: Where a match of the signature begins, uppercase hexadecimal: the address minus offset.

offset.description: The distance in bytes from patternStart to the address; inject at match+offset.

matchCount.description: How many matches the verification scan found; 2 means at least 2. Omitted when not verified.

triedPattern.description: Cheat Engine's last attempt when it found no unique signature, when it reported one.

name: asm_apply
title: Apply Auto Assembler patch
description: Apply a complete Auto Assembler patch and retain the Client-owned DISABLE lease. The script must contain ENABLE and DISABLE sections; the server classifies its commands and enforces the required capability switches before application. A failed apply can have an unknown partial effect, so inspect the target and use asm_release_patch whenever a lease was returned.

script.description: A complete rollback-capable Auto Assembler script, up to 1048576 characters.

name.description: An optional diagnostic patch name, up to 256 characters.

retained.description: Whether the patch was applied and retained by this MCP activation.

patchId.description: The patch id when retained, or the failed attempt id when Client ownership could not be retained.

appliedAfterTargetChange.description: Whether the selected target changed during application.

requiresManualRecovery.description: Whether recovery in Cheat Engine may be needed before changing the target.

release.description: The release outcome when ownership could not be retained.

hostEffect.description: The actual host effect of that release attempt.

hostWarnings.description: The bounded Auto Assembler warnings, when any.

hostWarningsTruncated.description: Whether hostWarnings was truncated by CheatEngine.Client.

name: asm_apply_code_patch
title: Apply code patch
description: Apply a generated code patch that asserts the expected original bytes before writing replacement bytes, and restores exactly those bytes through the Client-owned DISABLE lease. expectedBytes and replacementBytes must have the same 1 to 64 byte length. Release the returned patch id before selecting another process.

address.description: The address or expression of the first original byte.

expectedBytes.description: The expected original bytes, hexadecimal with optional spaces, 1 to 64 bytes.

replacementBytes.description: The replacement bytes, hexadecimal with optional spaces and the same length as expectedBytes.

name.description: An optional diagnostic patch name, up to 256 characters.

retained.description: Whether the patch was applied and retained by this MCP activation.

patchId.description: The patch id when retained, or the failed attempt id when Client ownership could not be retained.

appliedAfterTargetChange.description: Whether the selected target changed during application.

requiresManualRecovery.description: Whether recovery in Cheat Engine may be needed before changing the target.

release.description: The release outcome when ownership could not be retained.

hostEffect.description: The actual host effect of that release attempt.

hostWarnings.description: The bounded Auto Assembler warnings, when any.

hostWarningsTruncated.description: Whether hostWarnings was truncated by CheatEngine.Client.

name: asm_assemble
title: Assemble instructions
description: Assemble 1 to 128 instructions with CheatEngine.Client's typed instruction API. Nothing is written to target memory. Each next instruction begins after the bytes produced by the previous one, so relative operands use their actual origin.

instructions.description: The instruction sources, 1 to 128 entries, each at most 4096 characters.

preference.description: The preferred encoding for relative jumps and calls: None, Short, Long or Far.

skipRangeCheck.description: Whether Cheat Engine skips relative-branch reachability checks.

address.description: The origin used for this instruction, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

bytes.description: The assembled bytes, uppercase hexadecimal without separators.

size.description: The assembled byte count.

bytes.description: The concatenated bytes, uppercase hexadecimal without separators.

size.description: The total assembled byte count.

name: asm_check
title: Check Auto Assembler
description: Check an Auto Assembler ENABLE section without applying it. The server classifies the submitted source before Cheat Engine sees it and requires every capability it reaches. A successful check neither applies a patch nor proves a later apply will succeed.

script.description: A complete Auto Assembler source with ENABLE and DISABLE sections, up to 1048576 characters.

name.description: An optional diagnostic patch name, up to 256 characters.

accepted.description: Whether Cheat Engine accepted the ENABLE section. A true result does not apply the patch.

hostMessages.description: Cheat Engine's bounded, unparsed diagnostic text when it returned any.

hostMessagesTruncated.description: Whether hostMessages was truncated by CheatEngine.Client.

name: asm_generate_api_hook
title: Generate API hook
description: Ask Cheat Engine to generate an Auto Assembler API-hook script without applying it. Review the generated source, including its DISABLE path, and run asm_check before an explicit asm_apply.

address.description: The hook address expression.

newCallAddress.description: An optional symbol for the generated new-call address.

extension.description: An optional architecture extension passed to Cheat Engine.

targetSelf.description: Whether Cheat Engine should generate a hook in its own process.

script.description: The generated Auto Assembler source. Review, check and explicitly apply it separately.

expectedBytes.description: The validated original bytes asserted before an injection writes its jump; empty when Cheat Engine generated an API-hook script.

symbolName.description: The symbol the script registers while enabled, when generated as an injection.

name: asm_generate_injection
title: Generate AOB injection
description: Generate a rollback-capable AOB injection scaffold without applying it. It asserts the original bytes, allocates only while enabled, restores the bytes and releases its allocation and symbol while disabled. signature must be a verified unique module signature from aob_generate_signature; review the template, then use asm_check before any apply.

module.description: The loaded module name to scan, such as game.exe.

signature.description: A verified unique AOB signature from aob_generate_signature.

expectedBytes.description: The exact original instruction bytes asserted before the jump, at least 5 and at most 64 bytes.

symbolName.description: The Auto Assembler symbol name, 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits or underscores and not starting with a digit.

script.description: The generated Auto Assembler source. Review, check and explicitly apply it separately.

expectedBytes.description: The validated original bytes asserted before an injection writes its jump; empty when Cheat Engine generated an API-hook script.

symbolName.description: The symbol the script registers while enabled, when generated as an injection.

name: asm_list_patches
title: List Auto Assembler patches
description: List Auto Assembler patches whose Client leases are retained by this MCP activation. These patches block a process change until released, and never include patches created outside this activation.

patches.description: Client-owned patches held by this MCP activation, ordered by patch id.

selectionEpoch.description: The Client selection epoch where the patch was applied.

appliedAfterTargetChange.description: Whether the Client observed a changed selection immediately after applying the patch.

canDisable.description: Whether the Client can still run the original DISABLE section.

requiresManualRecovery.description: Whether the patch may need manual recovery.

hostWarnings.description: The bounded Auto Assembler warnings Cheat Engine returned, when any.

hostWarningsTruncated.description: Whether hostWarnings was truncated by CheatEngine.Client.

name: asm_release_patch
title: Release Auto Assembler patch
description: Run the original DISABLE section for one MCP-owned patch. A failed or target-changed release can leave a patch in the old target and require manual recovery; retry only when retryable is true. A successful release removes the patch from runtime resources.

patchId.description: The patch id returned by asm_apply or asm_apply_code_patch.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the release can still help.

requiresManualRecovery.description: Whether the patch may remain and needs manual recovery.

name: code_clear_dissect
title: Clear code dissect
description: Clear Cheat Engine's current code-dissector references, functions and strings. It refuses while an MCP code dissect job runs, because clearing during that native pass would make its output indeterminate.

cleared.description: Whether Cheat Engine completed the clear operation.

name: code_decode
title: Decode an instruction
description: Decode one target instruction through CheatEngine.Client and return Cheat Engine's columns, exact bytes and exact length. Use code_disassemble when surrounding instructions are needed.

address.description: An instruction address or Cheat Engine expression.
The instruction address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

opcode.description: The mnemonic and operands as Cheat Engine displayed them.

size.description: The instruction's positive byte length.

name: code_disassemble
title: Disassemble code
description: Disassemble 1 to 1024 target instructions with CheatEngine.Client's typed instruction API. before asks Cheat Engine for estimated predecessor boundaries, so it is useful for context but cannot prove a variable-length instruction boundary. The returned bytes are read from target memory in the same Client operation.

address.description: An instruction address or Cheat Engine expression, such as game.exe+1C0.

instructions.description: The instructions, from the earliest requested predecessor through the final instruction.

opcode.description: The mnemonic and operands as Cheat Engine displayed them.

kind.description: The failure class, such as memory_read_failed or not_found.

name: memory_hash
title: Hash memory
description: Hash a target range of up to 64 MiB with MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256, for example to detect that code or data changed. Reads 1 MiB per Cheat Engine dispatch and fails with target_changed if Cheat Engine selects another process in between; an unreadable byte fails with memory_read_failed.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression.

size.description: The number of bytes to hash, 1 to 67108864.

algorithm.description: The hash algorithm: md5, sha1 or sha256.

address.description: The resolved address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

size.description: The number of bytes hashed.

hash.description: The digest as lowercase hexadecimal without separators.

name: memory_list_regions
title: List memory regions
description: List the target's memory regions in address order, one page at a time, filtered by address range, module, state (committed by default), backing and the writable, executable and copy-on-write flags. The detailed format adds the allocation base, allocation protection and mapped file.

startAddress.description: Keep only regions that end after this address or expression; use with endAddress or alone.

endAddress.description: Keep only regions that start at or before this address or expression.

module.description: Keep only regions inside this loaded module's image, such as game.exe.

state.description: The region state to keep: committed (default), reserved, free or any.

writable.description: Whether regions must be writable: required, excluded or any (default).

executable.description: Whether regions must be executable: required, excluded or any (default).

copyOnWrite.description: Whether regions must be copy-on-write: required, excluded or any (default).

type.description: The backing to keep: image, mapped, private or any (default).

offset.description: The zero-based index of the first region to return.

limit.description: The most regions to return, 1 to 2000.

format.description: concise (default) or detailed, which adds allocation base, allocation protection and mapped file.

total.description: How many regions match the filters.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted when this page ends the listing.

truncated.description: Whether a host-side cap shortened the region map itself.

regions.description: The regions of this page, in address order.

base.description: The region's base address, uppercase hexadecimal.

size.description: The region's size in bytes.

state.description: The region's state: committed, reserved, free or unknown.

read.description: Whether the pages can be read.

write.description: Whether the pages can be written, copy-on-write included.

execute.description: Whether the pages can be executed.

copyOnWrite.description: Whether a write gives the process a private copy of the page.

type.description: The region's backing: image, mapped, private, none or unknown.

module.description: The loaded module whose image contains the region, when there is one.

allocationBase.description: The base of the allocation the region belongs to; detailed format only.

allocationProtection.description: The access the allocation was created with; detailed format only.

read.description: Whether the pages can be read.

write.description: Whether the pages can be written, copy-on-write included.

execute.description: Whether the pages can be executed.

copyOnWrite.description: Whether a write gives the process a private copy of the page.

mappedFile.description: Cheat Engine's description of the mapped file, when it reports one; detailed format only.

name: memory_load_from_file
title: Load memory from a file
description: Write a local file of 1 to 256 MiB into target memory. The absolute local path is checked and pinned against changes; MCP data and registry paths are refused. Writes run in blocks of at most 1 MiB. A failure reports the confirmed written prefix, including when the selected target changes; inspect memory before retrying.

address.description: Destination address or Cheat Engine address expression.

path.description: Absolute path of the local file on the Cheat Engine host.

name: memory_read
title: Read memory
description: Read target memory at one address: one typed value, up to 1024 consecutive values of a fixed-size type (count), a string (length) or raw bytes (size). Values are text: decimal integers, round-trippable floats, hexadecimal pointers, spaced hexadecimal bytes. An unreadable address fails with memory_read_failed.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression, such as game.exe+1C, [game.exe+10]+8 or 7FF6A1B2C3D0.

valueType.description: The value type to read.

count.description: How many consecutive values of a fixed-size type to read, 1 to 1024; only 1 for string, wstring and bytes.

size.description: The byte count for valueType bytes, 1 to 16384; refused for other types.

length.description: The maximum string length for string and wstring, 1 to 4096 (default 256); refused for other types.

address.description: The resolved address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

valueType.description: The value type that was read.

value.description: The value as text when count is 1: decimal integers, round-trippable floats, a hexadecimal pointer, the text of a string or spaced hexadecimal bytes.

values.description: The consecutive values in address order when count is above 1.

name: memory_read_batch
title: Read many addresses
description: Read up to 1024 addresses, each with its own value type, in one call (256 KiB in total). Fixed-size types are read in typed batches; an address that does not resolve or cannot be read reports its own error in band while the others are still read, so check every item.

items.description: The addresses to read, 1 to 1024, each with its value type and, for bytes or strings, its size or length.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression, such as game.exe+1C or 7FF6A1B2C3D0.

valueType.description: The value type to read.

size.description: The byte count, 1 to 16384; required for bytes and refused for other types.

length.description: The maximum string length, 1 to 4096 (default 256); only for string and wstring.

failed.description: How many items carry an error instead of a value; check every item.

items.description: One entry per request item, in request order.

address.description: The resolved address in uppercase hexadecimal, or the request text when it did not resolve.

value.description: The value as text, when it was read.

error.description: Why this item was not read; the other items are unaffected.

kind.description: The failure class, such as memory_read_failed or not_found.

name: memory_set_protection
title: Set memory protection
description: Change the page protection of up to 16 MiB of target memory (Cheat Engine's setMemoryProtection, or fullAccess when read, write and execute are all set). The entire range must fit in one committed memory region, so its returned previous access can restore the range. Change protection only with consent and restore previous when done.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression.

size.description: The number of bytes whose pages change, 1 to 16777216; all must fit in one committed memory region.

read.description: Whether the pages can be read.

write.description: Whether the pages can be written.

execute.description: Whether the pages can be executed.

address.description: The resolved address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

size.description: The size of the changed range in bytes.

previous.description: The access of every page before the change; restore the whole range with this tool using it.

read.description: Whether the page can be read.

write.description: Whether the page can be written.

execute.description: Whether the page can be executed.

current.description: The access of the first page after the change; compare it with the request, as some systems refuse write and execute together.

read.description: Whether the page can be read.

write.description: Whether the page can be written.

execute.description: Whether the page can be executed.

name: memory_write
title: Write memory
description: Write one typed value, a string or bytes to target memory. The first 64 bytes of the range are read first and returned as previous, so the write can be undone with valueType bytes; with verify the written bytes are read back. A wrong write can crash the target: write only addresses you identified, one at a time.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression, such as game.exe+1C or 7FF6A1B2C3D0.

valueType.description: The value type to write.

value.description: The value as text: decimal or 0x hexadecimal integers, invariant floats (NaN, Infinity), a hexadecimal pointer, the text of a string or spaced hexadecimal bytes such as 90 90.

repeat.description: How many times to write the bytes back to back, 1 to 65536 (1 MiB in total); only for bytes.

nullTerminate.description: Whether to append a terminating zero character; only for string and wstring.

verify.description: Whether to read the range back and compare it with the written bytes.

address.description: The resolved address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

previous.description: The first bytes the range held before the write, at most 64, as spaced hexadecimal; write them back with valueType bytes to undo.

verified.description: Whether a read-back matched every written byte; false when verify was off or another writer changed the range.

name: memory_write_batch
title: Write many addresses
description: Write up to 1024 addresses in request order, each with its own value type (1 MiB in total). Every address is resolved before the first write. The writes are not atomic: a failure stops the batch and reports partial_effect with completed, failedIndex and effectState, and the completed items stay written.

items.description: The writes, 1 to 1024, each with its address, value type and value.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression, such as game.exe+1C or 7FF6A1B2C3D0.

valueType.description: The value type to write.

value.description: The value as text: decimal or 0x hexadecimal integers, invariant floats, a hexadecimal pointer, the text of a string or spaced hexadecimal bytes.

verify.description: Whether to read every item back after the batch and list the items that differ.

written.description: How many items were written, all of them on success.

verified.description: Whether a read-back matched every item; false when verify was off or an item differs.

mismatched.description: The indices of the items whose read-back differs from the written bytes.

name: module_find_patches
title: Find module patches
description: Compare one module's executable sections in memory with its file on disk, after applying the file's base relocations, and report each differing range with its address, Cheat Engine name, file bytes and memory bytes: hooks, code patches and MCP or Cheat Engine injections. Read-only, in 256 KiB chunks; at most 64 MiB per call. The module's file must be on a local fixed drive (UNC, device and linked paths are refused) and must be the build that was loaded. The import address table is skipped; includeNonExecutable also compares data sections, which a running program changes on its own.

module.description: The module name, such as game.exe, or an address expression inside it.

includeNonExecutable.description: Also compare non-executable sections; they change at run time, so expect many differences.

limit.description: The most differing ranges to report, 1 to 1024.

filePath.description: The module file that was compared.

unreadableBytes.description: How many bytes of the module's memory could not be read and were skipped.

relocationsApplied.description: How many base relocations were applied to the file bytes before comparing.

truncated.description: Whether the scan stopped at limit patches or at the 64 MiB comparison cap.

address.description: The first differing address as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

section.description: The section that holds the range, such as .text.

length.description: The length of the range in bytes; runs closer than four bytes are merged.

fileBytes.description: The file's bytes after relocation, at most the first 64.

memoryBytes.description: The bytes in memory, at most the first 64.

symbol.description: Cheat Engine's name for the address, such as game.exe+1A2B; omitted when it has none.

name: module_get
title: Get module details
description: Read one module of the attached process: base, size, file path, its sections (with executable and writable flags) and the fields of its mapped PE header: machine, COFF time stamp, entry point, subsystem, DLL and .NET flags and the PDB it names. The time stamp identifies the build, so keep it to tell later whether the game was updated. module is a name such as game.exe (case-insensitive) or any address expression inside the module.

module.description: The module name, such as game.exe, or an address expression inside it, such as game.exe+1000.

base.description: The base address as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

path.description: The module's file on disk, as Cheat Engine reports it.

sections.description: The module's sections, as Cheat Engine enumerates them.

address.description: The section address as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

size.description: The section size in bytes.

fileOffset.description: The section's offset in the module file, as uppercase hexadecimal.

executable.description: Whether the PE header marks the section as code or executable; omitted when unknown.

writable.description: Whether the PE header marks the section writable; omitted when unknown.

size.description: The mapped size in bytes, when Cheat Engine reports it.

pe.description: The PE header fields; omitted when the mapped header cannot be read or parsed.

machine.description: The CPU the image targets: x86, x64, arm, arm64 or unknown.

timeDateStamp.description: The raw COFF time stamp as uppercase hexadecimal; it identifies a build, and reproducible builds store a hash in it.

headerImageBase.description: The ImageBase field of the mapped header; Windows usually rewrites it to the load address, so it is not the file's preferred base.

subsystem.description: The subsystem, such as windows_gui or windows_cui.

isDll.description: Whether the image is a DLL.

managed.description: Whether the image has a CLR header, which marks a .NET assembly.

timeDateStampUtc.description: The time stamp read as seconds since 1970 in UTC; omitted when it is zero.

entryPoint.description: The entry point address as uppercase hexadecimal; omitted when the image has none.

pdb.description: The PDB the image names in its CodeView record; omitted when it names none.

path.description: The PDB path recorded at link time.

signature.description: The PDB signature GUID, uppercase with dashes.

age.description: The PDB age; a symbol server keys the PDB by GUID and age.

name: module_list
title: List modules
description: Page the modules (EXE and DLLs) loaded in the attached process, or in another process by processId, in Cheat Engine's order. concise returns name, base and size; detailed adds is64Bit and the file path. Filter with nameContains, then page with offset and limit (at most 1000). Use it to classify the runtime (mono, GameAssembly, coreclr) and to find a module for module_get.

nameContains.description: A case-insensitive substring of the module name, such as mono or .dll; at most 256 characters.

offset.description: The index of the first module to return.

limit.description: The most modules to return, 1 to 1000.

format.description: concise (name, base, size) or detailed (adds is64Bit and path).

processId.description: The process whose modules are listed.

total.description: The number of modules that match nameContains.

modules.description: The modules of this page, in Cheat Engine's order.

name.description: The module name, such as game.exe.

base.description: The base address as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

size.description: The mapped size in bytes, when Cheat Engine reports it.

is64Bit.description: Whether the module is 64-bit; only with format detailed.

path.description: The module's file on disk; only with format detailed.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted on the last page.

name: module_list_exports
title: List module exports
description: Page the exports of one module of the attached process, parsed from its export directory in memory: name (omitted for ordinal-only exports), ordinal and address, or the forwarder such as NTDLL.RtlAllocateHeap for a forwarded export. Filter with nameContains, then page with offset and limit (at most 1000). A module whose export data exceeds 8 MiB or 65536 entries is refused.

module.description: The module name, such as kernel32.dll, or an address expression inside it.

nameContains.description: A case-insensitive substring of the export name; at most 256 characters.

offset.description: The index of the first export to return.

limit.description: The most exports to return, 1 to 1000.

total.description: The number of exports that match nameContains.

exports.description: The exports of this page, by ordinal.

name.description: The export name; omitted for an ordinal-only export.

address.description: The function address as uppercase hexadecimal; omitted for a forwarder.

forwarder.description: The forwarder, such as NTDLL.RtlAllocateHeap, when the export forwards to another module.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted on the last page.

name: mono_attach
title: Attach Mono collector
description: Inject Cheat Engine's Mono data collector. It can patch mono_error_ok, install Cheat Engine hooks, set the table Uses Mono option and show a native dialog; it may block for several seconds.

name: mono_compile_method
title: Compile Mono method
description: Ask the target Mono runtime to JIT-compile a method and return its native address. The address changes each run; this can execute runtime compilation work in the target.

name: mono_detach
title: Detach Mono collector
description: Close the Mono collector connection owned by this plugin activation and remove its hooks. The injected collector DLL and the mono_error_ok patch remain until the target restarts. An attachment from another Cheat Engine session is left unchanged.

name: mono_find_class
title: Find Mono class
description: Find a Mono class across the active collector images by exact namespace and class name.

namespace.description: The namespace; empty searches the global namespace.

name: mono_find_method
title: Find Mono method
description: Find the first Mono method with an exact name in a class. Inspect mono_list_methods first to resolve overloads.

name: mono_get_static_field_address
title: Get Mono static field address
description: Read a Mono class's static field-data base address. Add an individual static field's offset from mono_list_fields to reach that field.

domainHandle.description: An optional opaque Mono domain handle; the first domain is used when omitted.

name: mono_get_status
title: Get Mono collector status
description: Report whether Cheat Engine's Mono collector is attached and whether it reports its limited IL2CPP mode.

il2Cpp.description: Whether Cheat Engine reports its limited IL2CPP mode.

collectorVersion.description: The collector version when Cheat Engine reports it.

name: mono_invoke_method
title: Invoke Mono method
description: Invoke a Mono method once. It executes target code and can change game state or crash the target; a managed exception is returned in the result after the call ran. Use exact type codes from the method signature and never retry an uncertain result.

instanceAddress.description: The instance target address for an instance method; omit for a static method.

arguments.description: Arguments with Cheat Engine variable type codes and textual values.

value.description: The argument value as text; Cheat Engine converts it according to type.

name: mono_list_assemblies
title: List Mono assemblies
description: Page assemblies and their Mono images. Every handle is opaque and valid only while the collector remains attached.

offset.description: The zero-based first assembly.

name: mono_list_classes
title: List Mono classes
description: Page classes in a Mono image. Cheat Engine enumerates the image before applying the page, which can take time for large assemblies.

imageHandle.description: An opaque image handle from mono_list_assemblies.

offset.description: The zero-based first class.

name: mono_list_fields
title: List Mono fields
description: List up to 2048 fields of a Mono class, optionally including inherited fields. Offsets are relative to the object start.

includeParents.description: Include inherited fields when Cheat Engine supports the request.

name: mono_list_methods
title: List Mono methods
description: Page methods in a Mono class. Method handles are opaque and can be JIT-compiled with mono_compile_method.

offset.description: The zero-based first method.

jobId.description: The job id.

name: mono_start_instance_search
title: Start Mono instance search
description: Start a bounded lookup of possible instances for a Mono class. Cheat Engine scans for the class vtable in one job dispatch; poll it and stop it with runtime_stop_job before switching targets.

maximumResults.description: The maximum retained instance addresses, 1 to 2048.

lifetimeSeconds.description: How long the completed result remains pollable; the configured job maximum applies.

name: pointer_create_map
title: Create a pointer map
description: Starts a job that captures a pointer map: every aligned pointer-sized value that points into committed memory, read in short dispatches that recheck the selected process. Poll pointer_list_maps until state is ready; a changed process discards the map (target_changed). Stop it with pointer_delete_map or runtime_stop_job(jobId): a stopped map keeps what it read. The job ends at its TTL or a plugin disable; the map lives in this activation's memory until deleted, at most 4 maps and 8388608 pointers.

mapName.description: The new map's name, 1 to 128 characters.

endAddress.description: The last address to capture, inclusive; requires startAddress.

error.description: Why the capture failed or ended early.

name: pointer_delete_map
title: Delete a pointer map
description: Deletes a pointer map and frees its memory, stopping its capture job first when it still runs. Scans already found from the map keep their paths. An unknown name fails with not_found.

name.description: The deleted map or scan name.

cancelledJob.description: Whether its job was still running and was stopped.

name: pointer_delete_scan
title: Delete a pointer scan
description: Deletes a pointer scan and frees its paths, stopping its search job first when it still runs. An unknown name fails with not_found.

name.description: The deleted map or scan name.

cancelledJob.description: Whether its job was still running and was stopped.

name: pointer_find_paths

The job ends at its TTL or a plugin disable. Negative offsets and larger limits multiply the work; incomplete or traversalLimited with no path is no proof that none exists.

mapName.description: The pointer map to search; see pointer_list_maps.

target.description: The address the paths must reach: hexadecimal, or a symbol resolved in the selected process.

maxDepth.description: The most dereferences in a path, 1 to 8.

maxOffset.description: The largest offset after a dereference, 0 to 1048576 bytes.

maxNodes.description: The most candidate pointers visited, 1 to 10000000.

jobId.description: The search job's id, for runtime_list_jobs and runtime_stop_job.

elapsedMs.description: How long the search ran, in milliseconds.

A symbol marks a holder inside a module image, a static root.

maxOffset.description: The largest distance below target a pointer may point, 0 to 65536; 0 finds exact pointers.

unreadableBytes.description: How many requested bytes could not be read.

incomplete.description: Whether the capture skipped memory or stopped early; absence in the map is then no proof.

progressPercent.description: How much of the planned memory was read, 0 to 100.

error.description: Why the capture failed or ended early.

incomplete.description: Whether the scan may miss paths or keeps unverified ones.

base.description: The root address when the path was found, uppercase hexadecimal.

offsets.description: The offsets in dereference order, signed hexadecimal.

verification.description: How the path was last verified: snapshot_match, live_match or unresolved.

module.description: The root's module, when a module holds the root; rescans rebase it by name.

moduleOffset.description: The root's offset in its module, uppercase hexadecimal, when a module holds the root.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted on the last page.

name: pointer_list_scans

state.description: Where the search stands; the paths are usable when ready, stopped or expired.

incomplete.description: Whether the paths may miss some: an incomplete map, a limit, a stop or unresolved paths.

traversalLimited.description: Whether maxNodes or maxResults stopped the search.

visitedNodes.description: How many candidate pointers were visited.

description: Resolve up to 256 Cheat Engine expressions in one call. Each entry returns the address, Cheat Engine's best name for it (module+offset or symbol) and the symbol record when the expression names one. An expression that does not resolve carries its own error; check every entry. shallow skips the slower lookups, such as symbols still loading.

description: Inspect and load a .CT, .XML or .CETRAINER file through CheatEngine.Client. The source is pinned while inspected and loaded, and Client independently enforces CheatEngineClient:AllowedTableRoots. The inspection derives and enforces capability gates before Cheat Engine can execute Lua, Auto Assembler records or a Mono auto attach. A native load failure can leave a partial table or script effect.

path.description: The absolute local table path. CheatEngineClient:AllowedTableRoots must admit it.

merge.description: Whether to merge into the existing address list rather than replace it.

path.description: The absolute table path admitted by CheatEngine.Client's allowed table roots.

merge.description: Whether Cheat Engine merged the table into the existing address list.

inspection.description: The inspection that ran while the source file was pinned.

format.description: xml when completely inspected, or the opaque format that forced a conservative policy.

containsLua.description: Whether a Lua script is present or the table could not be inspected.

containsForms.description: Whether forms are present or the table could not be inspected.

usesMono.description: Whether the table sets UsesMono or could not be inspected.

recordCount.description: The CheatEntry count for an inspected XML table; zero for an opaque table.

assemblerScriptCount.description: The Auto Assembler script count for an inspected XML table; zero for an opaque table.

requires.description: The feature switches this particular table required and the tool enforced before loading it.

monoAutoAttach.description: Whether this load could trigger Cheat Engine's Mono data-collector auto attach.

name: table_save
title: Save cheat table
description: Save the current table through CheatEngine.Client to a .CT, .XML or .CETRAINER path under CheatEngineClient:AllowedTableRoots. overwrite must be true when a destination file already exists. A native save failure can leave a partially written destination.

path.description: The absolute destination table path inside CheatEngineClient:AllowedTableRoots.

overwrite.description: Whether an existing destination may be replaced.

path.description: The absolute table destination admitted by CheatEngine.Client's allowed table roots.

replacedExisting.description: Whether a file existed at the destination immediately before the save began.

name: util_calculate
title: Calculate a 64-bit expression
description: Evaluate an integer expression with unsigned 64-bit wraparound. Literals are decimal or 0x hexadecimal. Supported operators are + - * / % << >> & ^ | ~ and parentheses; division is unsigned and division by zero is refused.

expression.description: An unsigned 64-bit expression up to 4096 characters, such as (0x7FF60000 + 0x1C0) - 8.

unsignedValue.description: The resulting 64-bit bit pattern in invariant unsigned decimal.

signedValue.description: The same 64-bit bit pattern interpreted as signed two's-complement decimal.

hex.description: The same bit pattern as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

name: util_convert_value
title: Convert a value
description: Convert a bounded value through its byte representation without accessing the target. Numeric and pointer bytes are presented in the requested byte order; UTF-8 and UTF-16 strings keep their encoding order. The source and target scalar byte counts must match.

value.description: The input value, using the same text syntax as memory_read and memory_write.

sourceType.description: The type used to parse value.

targetType.description: The type used to decode the converted bytes.

byteOrder.description: The byte order to use when presenting scalar bytes.

pointerSize.description: The pointer width for pointer inputs or outputs: 4 or 8.

sourceType.description: The value type used to parse the input.

targetType.description: The value type used to decode the converted bytes.

byteOrder.description: The requested order of scalar bytes in bytes; string encodings keep their defined UTF byte order.

pointerSize.description: The pointer width used for pointer inputs or outputs, 4 or 8.

bytes.description: The converted bytes, uppercase hexadecimal pairs separated by spaces.

value.description: The target value represented by bytes.
